claims.claim: Augustine of Hippo was a Christian theologian and philosopher who served as Bishop of Hippo Regius from 396 to 430.
Augustine was born in 354 in Thagaste, Numidia (in Roman Africa, modern Algeria) and died in 430.
Before his conversion to Christianity, Augustine was a 'hearer' (auditor) of Manichaeism for about nine years, beginning around 373.
Against the Epistle of Manichaeus Called Fundamental was written in A.D. 397.
The work is directed against a letter that served as a type of catechism of the Manichaean sect.
In this work, Augustine refutes the letter's commencement and general principles by showing that Mani has no reason to refer to Christ and by illustrating the absurdity of Manichaean dualism.
At the beginning of his episcopate, Augustine devoted himself to refuting Manichaeanism, including publicly debating the Manichaean Felix in 404.
The Latin title of the work is Contra Epistolam Manichaei quam vocant Fundamenti.
Augustine is generally regarded as one of the most influential philosophers in the history of the Western world and one of the most important Church Fathers of the Latin Church.
